question: Two children present with diarrhoea. A 5-year-old has 3 weeks of foul-smelling, greasy, non-bloody stools with abdominal bloating and no fever — stool microscopy shows pear-shaped flagellate trophozoites. A 6-year-old has bloody mucoid diarrhoea with tenesmus and low-grade fever — stool microscopy shows erythrophagocytic trophozoites. What is the correct treatment for each child respectively?

answers.text: Both children should receive metronidazole as it treats both Giardia and Entamoeba

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While metronidazole treats both, it is the first-line only for amoebiasis. For giardiasis, tinidazole is preferred as first-line due to superior cure rates, shorter course, and better tolerability.

answers.text: 5-year-old (giardiasis) = tinidazole; 6-year-old (amoebiasis) = metronidazole followed by a luminal agent (diloxanide furoate)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Giardia lamblia (pear-shaped flagellate) → tinidazole (single dose, superior cure rate) or metronidazole. Entamoeba histolytica (erythrophagocytic trophozoite = amoebae containing ingested red blood cells, pathognomonic) → metronidazole to eliminate tissue trophozoites, followed by a luminal agent (diloxanide furoate) to eradicate cysts in the colon and prevent relapse/transmission.

Incorrect. Albendazole has modest activity against Giardia but is not first-line. More importantly, tinidazole alone for amoebiasis does not clear intraluminal cysts — a luminal agent (diloxanide furoate) is needed after tissue-active treatment to prevent relapse and cyst shedding.

Incorrect. Giardiasis requires specific antiprotozoal therapy (tinidazole or metronidazole) — ORS alone will not eliminate the parasite. For uncomplicated intestinal amoebiasis without perforation, oral metronidazole is adequate; IV is reserved for severe amoebic dysentery or extraintestinal disease.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the parasitic infection management section. Key treatments: Giardia = tinidazole (preferred) or metronidazole. E. histolytica (amoebiasis) = metronidazole + diloxanide furoate (luminal agent to clear cysts). The erythrophagocytic trophozoite is the pathognomonic feature of invasive amoebiasis.

Correct. Giardiasis → tinidazole (first-line). Amoebiasis → metronidazole (tissue) + diloxanide furoate (luminal). The erythrophagocytic trophozoite (RBC-containing amoeba) is pathognomonic of invasive E. histolytica.
